title: Drop and Protocol
premise: Emrys Pemberton, a peace-delegation interpreter haunted by a botched translation that got a colleague killed, receives a meeting request from that dead handler's account. Following it, she learns the handler faked his death to expose Protocol Vellum, an inheritance scheme in which intelligence assets are passed down like property through compromised families—including her own. Tasked with extracting a defector who may be bait to flush out the network, Emrys must decide whether loyalty to her handlers or the truth serves her better. In the end she delivers the defector, burns the Protocol's ledger from inside the negotiation itself, and accepts a new identity built on the truth she once buried.
about_author: Bram Coldharbour is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind glass booths in cities where ceasefires were signed and quietly broken. He writes thrillers about people whose words carry consequences they never agreed to.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Emrys Pemberton, running on four hours of sleep, interprets a fractious ceasefire session in Geneva while dodging questions about her colleague Aldous Wren's death three months ago. That night, her secure inbox pings: a meeting invitation from Wren's account, timestamped for tomorrow. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into forbidden hope.

chapters.title: Booth Nine
chapters.summary: Emrys verifies the invitation is authentic—Wren's old cipher, his private jokes—and goes to a shuttered interpreting booth at the abandoned Palais annex. A recording plays: Wren alive until recently, warning her that Protocol Vellum treats agents as inheritable assets, and that her family name appears in its ledger. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: vertigo—her invisibility was always someone else's design.

chapters.title: The Defector Who Smiles
chapters.summary: Delegation security chief Ivo Marchetti assigns Emrys to handle Marek Vasik, a signals officer defecting with proof of Vellum. Vasik is charming, fluent, and keeps testing whether Emrys recognizes names from Wren's recording. She realizes her assignment wasn't coincidence—someone placed her. POV Emrys, with one interlude of Vasik's coded report home. Emotional beat: paranoia wearing a professional smile.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Emrys breaks into her late mother's effects and finds a Vellum succession letter naming her as third-generation asset, recruited before she could consent. Flashbacks reveal her childhood 'language tutor' was a handler. She confronts what loyalty to the service has actually cost. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: grief curdling into fury.

chapters.title: Safe House Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Moving Vasik between safe houses, Emrys counts the surveillance patterns and concludes the route was leaked—by Marchetti or by Vasik himself. A tail forces an improvised escape through the old town; Vasik saves her life, complicating her suspicion. POV alternating Emrys/Vasik. Emotional beat: trust as a calculated gamble neither can afford.

chapters.title: What Wren Buried
chapters.summary: Following Wren's dead-drop instructions, Emrys recovers his ledger fragment: Vellum's beneficiaries include the delegation's own mediators—the peace process exists to launder the inheritance network. Wren's last note asks her forgiveness for using her as the key. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Vasik confesses: he was sent by Vellum to test whether Emrys would activate as an asset—or burn. But he's flipped, carrying genuine evidence, because Vellum killed his brother for trying to exit. They must decide together whether extraction is rescue or delivery into a trap. POV Vasik primarily. Emotional beat: two liars choosing truth as strategy.

chapters.title: Marchetti's Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys confronts Marchetti, who reveals he's been running a counter-operation since Wren's death but needs her—only a registered Vellum asset can access the closing session's sealed annex where the master ledger is exchanged. He offers her the choice he never had. POV Marchetti, then Emrys. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, the weight of being indispensable.

chapters.title: Closing Session
chapters.summary: During the treaty's final plenary, Emrys interprets on the record while covertly triggering the annex exchange, letting Marchetti's team take the ledger mid-handoff. Vellum's inside man—her mother's old handler—tries to trigger a kill protocol; Vasik draws him off at cost of his own cover. POV Emrys under pressure. Emotional beat: climax—every word she speaks is both shield and weapon.

chapters.title: Drop and Protocol
chapters.summary: The network unravels quietly; some names are prosecuted, most are retired. Emrys testifies under a protection protocol, then declines reinstatement, taking a new name and a teaching post far from the booths. She finally sleeps through the night—then wakes, and chooses to answer a knock at the door anyway. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: resolution—inherited silence ends with her.
